newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican firm awarded $120 mln telecom project.
newsitem.headline: Mexican firm awarded $120 mln telecom project.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Telecommunications Commission has awarded the privately-held firm PCM Communications a concession to install and operate an interstate telecommunications network, the Communications and Transport Ministry said on Wednesday.

The Mexican firm will be supported by the Swedish telecoms group LM Ericsson AB, which is providing part of the financing along with Swedish Export Credit Guarantee Board and Nordic Investment Bank, the ministry said in a statement.
The first phase of the project, to take place in 1997, is worth $120 million, the ministry said.

PCM has promised to establish telecommunications centres in the northern border cities of Tijuana and Nuevo Laredo, generating 2,000 direct and indirect jobs, the ministry said. The project is concentrating on northern border cities.
The fibre-optic network will connect 40 cities over 1,164 miles (1,878 km).
PCM is led by well-known Mexican investors Federico Wilkins, Roberto Salmeron and David Pons, who control 51 percent of the company, the ministry said.
The remainder is held by Communication Equity Associates, which specialises in telecommunications and cable televison.
